 07 Nov 2026 Arteta – ‘We can still do much better’
 Josh James 0
 0
 0
 0
 0
 0
 We secured our ninth win from our first ten league games of the season, equalling a club record, with a 1-0 victory over Hull City on Saturday – but Mikel Arteta said there is much more to come from his team. 
 Martin Odegaard’s second-half goal was enough to make it 27 points out of a possible 30 to start the campaign, a tally we have only previously managed once before in our history. 
 But despite the table-topping start to our Premier League defence, the manager believes the best is yet to come, and that improvements will come.
 “I think it's the first time, or second, in our history that we've done it, so that's the difficulty of that,” he said, “and the games that we have already played and the away games, but it's great. 
 “We can still be much better, and we will improve in many phases, and we will get certain relationships to a different level that will be even more efficient. That's the next step, to have bigger margins and when we have them, the opportunities, put them away to make sure that we don't have to hang in there the last few minutes.”
 It was also our third win in the space of a week, following trips away to Liverpool and Slavia Prague, and the manager added that Saturday’s performance should also be looked at in the context of the recent schedule. 
 “I need to praise the players,” Arteta said at full time, “the staff for what they've done in the last block of games because it's been extremely demanding. The level of the opponents, how quickly the games and how they were coming and the way we played and performed and to get results is just remarkable.”
 It’s the perfect way to head into the next international break, and in stark contrast to September when we lost to Brighton immediately before the international hiatus. Arteta said that the next two weeks will be especially important to help prepare for a challenging fixture list that waits for us later in the month – when we face Newcastle United, Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City before the December schedule.
 “It's a completely different break. After Brighton it was a long one, especially it was a long break, so now that one I'm going to enjoy. We're going to work to plan what is happening in the next month because when you see the games, the quality of games that we have to play, it's quite impressive. 
 “Let's make sure that we are prepared for that from our side, make sure that we are on top of the players to do the things that they have to do in the international teams. Make sure they enjoy it because it's an incredible opportunity for them as well and when we are back together, we'll go again.”
